page: Amazon Web Services t4g.large is a burstable general-purpose instance powered by the 64-bit Arm architecture. Built on the AWS Nitro System, the instance utilizes an AWS Graviton2 processor based on the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. It is configured with 2 physical cores and 2 vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz with one thread per core. Memory capacity is 8.0 GB, delivering 4.0 GB of RAM per core, backed by 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The instance features hardware AES cryptographic support but does not include AVX, AMX, or discrete GPUs. There is no bundled local storage, and baseline network throughput is rated at 1 Gbps.

Benchmark measurements reflect the burstable, dual-core design of the processor. Single-core compute capacity registered an average score of 1517.49 on stress-ng, while multi-core execution reached 3012.08, falling into the lower quartile. Geekbench scores reached 921.0 for single-core and 1697.0 for multi-core. Memory bandwidth tests produced 34.42 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 18.39 GB/sec for uncached write operations. In workload-specific benchmarks, the server achieved 2.19 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, 2.3 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, and 1272.83 in PassMark database operations.

The burstable credit model makes t4g.large an efficient resource choice for intermittent compute demands, allowing baseline resource reservation with burst capabilities when needed. However, the hardware presents clear tradeoffs: sustained peak utilization is constrained by the burst budget, and the absence of local disks requires external network storage. This profile matches lightweight web servers, microservices, continuous integration runners, staging environments, and low-concurrency database deployments.
description: Amazon Web Services t4g.large is an Arm-based general-purpose instance featuring a 2.5 GHz AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processor with 2 vCPUs, 2 physical cores, and 8.0 GB of memory. Operating under the AWS Nitro System, it provides a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio, hardware AES encryption, and a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place its single-core compute performance within the average band, while multi-core compute and memory bandwidth measure in lower tiers due to its dual-core configuration. Utilizing a burstable CPU credit allocation, t4g.large offers cost-efficient scaling for variable processing patterns. It is technically suited for development environments, low-traffic web serving, caching nodes, and light database workloads that do not require sustained 100% CPU loads.
